In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of mitochondrial respiration in the cells is a very complex phenomenon, and it is impossible to describe it by a single simple model.
the cellular metabolism is organized and regulated in a very sophisticated manner by means of compartmentation, substrate-product channellng, metabolic waves and feed-back loops.

metabolic regulation of respi-ration in muscle cells is based on substrate channelling, and that the role of cytosolic ADP in this process is not that of a conventional allosteric regulator, but is rather a signal of metabolic state of the whole muscle cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulation of respiration in muscle cells is not a simple feedback mechanism, but a complex system with a lot of feedbacks, feed-forwards and feed-backwards, and with a very high degree of compartmentation.

metabolic regulation of respi-ration is a complex phenomenon, which cannot be understood without taking into account the structural organization of the cell, compartmentation of metabolites and substrate-product chaneling.
the metabolic compartmentation is a very important factor of metabolic regulation and the cell interior should not be treated as homogenous solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cellular metabolism is not controlled by cytoplasmatic ADP, but rather by local concentration of creatine phosphate and ADP at the sites of ATP utilization and production, and that the mitochondrial creatine kinase system is a powerful regulator of mitochondrial respiration.
the cellular metabolism is not controlled by the cytoplasmic concentration of ADP, but by its local concentration and diffusion fluxes in structured cytoplasm.
metabolic compartmentation, multienzyme system organization and substrate channellingshould be considered in the future as important factors of cellular regulation of mitochondrial respiration.
